headline: 51 dead as floods and landslides batter Bangladesh
summary: Over 80,000 homes destroyed and one million people affected across seven districts following heavy rains and flash floods.
details: According to the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief, 44 people have died due to floods and landslides in the south-eastern and north-eastern regions of the country. However, recent reports indicate the death toll has risen to 51.

Cox's Bazar has been the hardest hit, with 28 deaths recorded, including 15 local residents and 13 Rohingya refugees. Chittagong district follows with 13 deaths, while Bandaranban and Rangamati have seen 6 and 3 deaths respectively.

The disaster has caused massive infrastructure damage, with 79,187 homes, 344 educational institutions, and 339 bridges and culverts destroyed. Additionally, 3,840 kilometers of roads have been damaged.
Currently, 34,723 people are taking shelter in 3,941 emergency shelters. A total of 408 unions have been submerged under water across the seven affected districts.

The disaster has caused massive infrastructure damage, with 79,187 homes, 344 educational institutions, and 339 bridges and culverts destroyed. Additionally, 3,840 kilometers of roads have been damaged.

headline: Head teacher attacks education official with axe in Shariatpur
summary: Jasim Uddin, an acting head teacher, was detained after allegedly attacking Upazila Assistant Primary Education Officer Shakil Ahmed with an axe in his office.
details: A shocking incident occurred Sunday afternoon at the Gosairhat Upazila Primary Education Office in Shariatpur, where an acting head teacher allegedly attacked an education official with an axe.

The accused, Jasim Uddin, is the acting head teacher of North Char Jalalpur Government Primary School. He is alleged to have attacked Upazila Assistant Primary Education Officer Shakil Ahmed due to a prior dispute.
According to police sources, Jasim Uddin entered the office wearing a raincoat, a mask, and sunglasses. He then pulled an axe from his bag and attacked Shakil Ahmed.
Other officials and staff present at the office quickly intervened to stop the attack and rescue the victim. The attacker was held by the staff until police arrived and detained him.
The injured official, Shakil Ahmed, received primary medical treatment at the Gosairhat Upazila Health Complex.

In a video recorded while in police custody, Jasim Uddin appeared to be speaking incoherently, claiming he had drunk a soft drink and watched an Argentina football match, stating he did not know what happened next.
